messages.content: ✅ click(Link:First Australian rare earth processing facility under construction The processing market is dominated by China, but Australia is building its capabilities in an attempt to boost the domestic industry. Australian Broadcasting Corporation · 1d): Success

The gist is: ANSTO (Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation) is building a state-owned pilot plant in Sydney to process rare earths found in clay deposits. This will help Aussie rare earth miners avoid building their own costly pilot plants — saving them millions and speeding up development by about six months.

Australian Rare Earths (AR3) will be the first to use it for their Koppamurra mining project in South Australia. The plant is meant to be a shared facility for multiple companies to kickstart their projects without the usual hassle.

Basically, it’s about getting a proper local setup to process rare earth minerals so Australia isn’t stuck relying on China’s dominance.

Want me to dig up more details or check the timeline for when it’ll be ready?
